summary: Bounded review of lower_compose plus its helpers sync_action and rewrite_component_item: dangling `internal` references are silently accepted despite the documented error contract, merged init meta is first-wins with silent drop of later blocks, and sync action names are not uniqueness-checked before reaching composed_kernel (outcome unverified).

findings.title: internal references to unknown aliases or actions are silently ignored instead of returning CoreError
findings.description: lower_compose collects ComposeItem::Internal { alias, action } pairs into the `internal` set (compose.rs:294-298) and uses it only to suppress matching exposed actions (compose.rs:326); the dispatch arm `ComposeItem::Internal { .. } => {}` (compose.rs:357) never checks that the alias names a used component or that the action exists in that component. A misspelled or dangling `internal a.foo` is therefore accepted with no diagnostic, and the action it was meant to hide (if it exists under the correct spelling) remains in the composed kernel's public action surface. This contradicts the function's documented contract: "Returns CoreError for missing/invalid components, unknown aliases or actions" (compose.rs:251-254). Concrete trigger: a compose document with `use a = "..."` plus `internal a.nonexistent` (or an alias that is never `use`d); lowering succeeds and the hiding request is a silent no-op.

findings.title: meta of later init blocks is silently dropped when multiple inits are merged into one
findings.description: When merging SpecItem::Init blocks (from components at compose.rs:310-324 and from ComposeItem::Common at compose.rs:340-350), `init_annotations` is accumulated from every block, but `init_meta` is only adopted from the first block seen via `if init_meta.is_none()` (compose.rs:320-322, 346-348). Meta from all subsequent init blocks is discarded with no error and no warning, even though the same function records diagnostics in `warnings` for other merge hazards (e.g. fair_not_inherited via sync_action, compose.rs:354-356) before calling composed_kernel. Concrete trigger: two used components, or a component plus a common block, each declaring an init with non-None meta; the composed SpecItem::Init (compose.rs:360-364) keeps only the first block's meta, silently losing the rest.

findings.title: sync action names are not uniqueness-checked before being pushed into the composed kernel
findings.description: sync_action builds the composite action with the user-supplied, unprefixed name `action.name` (compose.rs:1106-1115), and lower_compose pushes every sync action into `actions` (compose.rs:354-356, 365) with no duplicate-name check — in contrast to component aliases, which are rejected on duplication (compose.rs:273-275), and to rewrite_component_item, which prefix-qualifies component-level names with the alias (compose.rs:392, 430, 470). Two sync blocks with the same name in one compose document both reach composed_kernel. Whether composed_kernel rejects the duplicate is not decidable from the received projections because its source was never included, so the concrete outcome (silent shadowing of one body by the other, changing which statements run under that name) is unverified. Concrete trigger: one compose document containing two `sync` actions named `x`.

abstentions: Whether composed_kernel (source absent from all received projections) rejects duplicate action names or duplicate state fields — determines the final outcome of the sync-name collision finding.

Whether a sync action's reference list may legally contain the same constituent action twice; if legal, the per-reference unbounded `items.extend` (compose.rs:1081-1085) duplicating the constituent's statements is intended behavior rather than a defect.

Whether parse_component (compose.rs:51-154, card not expanded) rejects actions with duplicate parameter names; if it does, the last-wins binding from `collect::<HashMap<_, _>>` (compose.rs:1071-1080) is unreachable for duplicate-named parameters.
information_loss: Only declared cards could be expanded and the 3-expansion budget was spent on target-body, sync-alias-boundary, and component-rewrite-front, so parse_component, rewrite_compose_statements, rewrite_statements, resolve_alias_* / substitute_action_item, and the statement/expression/alias-resolution cards were never seen.
composed_kernel, FileResolver, SurfaceCompose/ComposeItem definitions, and the docs/LANGUAGE.md semantics are not present in any received projection.
No type resolution, tests, or runtime evidence were available; all findings are source-level claims from frozen line windows only.
